title: Design optimal Vouch system including adoption
description: Use the grill-with-docs decision-tree workflow to synthesize vouch mk2 internals, the existing vouch-mk2-system-diagram.html, mk1 lessons, and the adoption/implementation framework. Record settled domain language and hard-to-reverse architectural decisions, then revise the agreed system documentation only after the user confirms shared understanding.
design: Round 1 settled 2026-08-20: design an evolutionary target system with the proven mk2 assurance kernel and a product-owned adoption operating system; label implemented/piloted/proposed/adopter-owned/external elements. Beachhead is a technical lead or maintainer of a small agent-heavy GitHub team. Primary job is safer agent-assisted delivery; audit and standardization are secondary benefits. Scope is the full adoption lifecycle. Optimize brownfield-first with a greenfield fast lane. Preserve mk2's authority, purity, append-only history, content addressing, transition-gate, explicit-deviation, truthful-NOT_CHECKED, thin-adapter, and read-only-MCP principles; packaging, GitHub adapter, commands, schema and UI remain revisitable.
acceptance_criteria: All artifact-derived facts are reconciled; every reachable architecture, adoption, rollout, governance, and measurement decision branch is explicitly settled with the user; shared understanding is confirmed before edits; agreed documentation is updated and verified without overwriting unrelated work.
notes:
Rounds 1-8 are recorded in CONTEXT.md and prior bead history. Round 8 settled 2026-08-21: adoption-module failure cannot corrupt or reinterpret kernel results; health is recomputed locally without a daemon; event order is mechanical while unsupported wall-clock values remain claims; assessments are bounded and return incomplete on exhaustion; referenced history persists; notifications are local-only; enforcement outages never silently downgrade a hard gate. Round 9 settled 2026-08-21: preserve vouch-mk2-system-diagram.html; create vouch-system-diagram.html and vouch-optimal-system.md; show current, dogfooded, target, adopter-owned, and external-proof status honestly; document adoption and assurance as separate but composed flows; create only the agreed hard-to-reverse ADRs; verify the interactive diagram visually. Q74 settled 2026-08-21: optimal Vouch uses fail-closed hybrid incremental verification. Ordinary changes verify the affected closure from an exact verified baseline and reuse only locally stored results whose complete bound inputs are unchanged. Unmapped or global changes, missing or mismatched baselines, releases, recovery, upgrades, and explicit audits require full verification. Formal results are bound to exact Vouch, checker, model, and policy identity instead of rerunning for unrelated adopter code. No telemetry or remote cache is introduced. Canonical settled terms were added to CONTEXT.md. Q75-Q80 settled 2026-08-21: the per-scope reusable result is a verification capsule, distinct from the formal certificate. A human-confirmed scope manifest is authoritative; candidate automation may propose it but ambiguity fails closed. Capsules live only in the repository-local append-only content-addressed record and require an exact hard-gated baseline plus complete identity match; ephemeral caches cannot affect verdicts. The assurance kernel owns affected-closure planning, capsule validity, and composition; project policy declares scopes, dependencies, and commands; delivery adapters supply normalized change manifests and execute plans without deciding scope or claims. Incremental composition may support whole-project assurance when every scope and global obligation is accounted for, but reports distinguish it from full verification and expose baseline, head, affected/reused scopes, rationale, and last full revision. Ordinary cost scales with the affected closure; budget exhaustion is incomplete or NOT_CHECKED and blocks hard progression. CONTEXT.md was updated inline. Q81-Q88 settled 2026-08-21 with Q82 clarified by the user: release composition may use complete incremental composition, while full verification is triggered by global invalidation, missing trust, recovery, upgrades, audits, or declared cadence rather than every continuous-delivery release. Every relevant path has exactly one primary scope or explicit exclusion; purity versus effects changes dependency and integration obligations, not ownership. Shared behavior is modeled as its own primary scope, and effectful or cross-scope behavior as a first-class integration scope. Dependency contracts permit downstream reuse when unchanged; opaque dependencies conservatively propagate producer changes. The kernel independently binds adapter-supplied base, head, and path facts. Capsules bind all assurance inputs and identities semantically rather than expiring by time. Branch merges recompute closure from the exact common verified ancestor and never union green results blindly. The kernel emits immutable verification plans; local or delivery runner adapters may execute entries in parallel and return provenance-honest, plan-bound receipts. CONTEXT.md was updated inline. Q89-Q94 settled 2026-08-21: scope ownership remains path-level and single-primary-scope; independently governed behavior sharing a file belongs to a containing scope or should be split rather than introducing language-specific symbol ownership. The kernel is language-agnostic about purity and effects; mechanically produced effect facts may bind dependency contracts, but purity neither proves an unchanged contract nor does effectfulness imply global invalidation. Assurance policy limits full-verification distance by governed changes or releases, with projects able to tighten but not weaken tier requirements. Parallel plan attempts preserve all receipts; only complete successful scope execution creates a replacement capsule. Forge receipts bind exact change, plan, command, workflow/runner/toolchain, outcome, and output identity while reporting external attestation honestly and causing no Vouch telemetry. Full verification of all active scopes is distinct from a historical scrub of genesis-to-head events and evidence; incremental and full runs may validate a suffix from an exact verified checkpoint, while recovery, corruption, major upgrades, explicit history audits, and longer cadence trigger a historical scrub. CONTEXT.md was updated inline. Q95-Q102 settled 2026-08-21: a verified checkpoint binds exact history roots, state, schema, policy, verifier, and hard-gated repository revision and may extend only a trusted prefix through a verified suffix. Passed entries from a partial plan remain reusable only under the identical plan, tree, inputs, environment, and policy; retries append receipts and changes require a new plan. Ordinary incremental and full verification cover active scopes and claimed release rosters; historical scrubs cover retired and superseded history, and renewed old claims require current verification. Scope-manifest revisions are governed and use the union of impact under old and new mappings. Generated paths bind generator and inputs; vendored dependencies are explicit pinned scopes; exclusions cannot feed governed behavior. Cross-root consumers bind exact published dependency contracts and never share authority. Effectful scopes reuse only when effect inputs are fixed or mechanically bound; otherwise the relevant input and scope are volatile. Secret values are never stored or hashed; a non-secret version handle may be bound, otherwise execution remains volatile. CONTEXT.md was updated inline. Q103-Q109 settled 2026-08-21: greenfield projects establish a scope manifest, full verification, and historical scrub before reusable checkpoints; existing mk2 stores remain full-only after upgrade until human scope confirmation and explicit baseline establishment, with no synthesized retroactive capsules and permanent force-full availability. Retries are explicit, bounded, plan-identical, append-only, and visibly preserve instability. Incremental soundness is the central invariant: incremental composition never passes when full verification of the same supported state/change would fail; the bounded formal model and differential/property tests cover closure, capsules, checkpoints, invalidators, and merges.
